assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic peak is a calibrated standard ruler imprinted by sound waves in the primordial plasma, and its detection in galaxy clustering gives a clean, geometrically transparent handle on the expansion history and dark energy. This is nature supplying a clue about the dark sector rather than a clever model; it is among the cleanest cosmological measurements of the era.
assessment.attribution: The first detections of the peak in galaxy surveys (SDSS luminous red galaxies, 2dFGRS) were made by the Eisenstein and Cole groups; Sunyaev contributed the early theoretical identification of acoustic features in the matter distribution (with Zeldovich, and independently Peebles and Yu). Zeldovich is deceased, and the two survey teams are large collaborations, so assigning individuals is delicate but workable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently confirmed by SDSS/BOSS/eBOSS, WiggleZ, 6dF and now DESI, with consistent results across redshift. Interpretation is stable. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy are a reason the field is active, not a threat to the ruler itself. Timely, given the 2011 and 2019 prizes laid the groundwork.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would see this as sufficiently distinct from the 2011 acceleration discovery and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Credit split between the two survey teams and the theory pioneers (Peebles/Yu, Zeldovich) is contested and I am relying on recalled history rather than verification.
Recent DESI evolving-dark-energy results are not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos in the TeV-PeV range, then associating neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and with the Galactic plane. It is a real new window on the universe and an engineering feat at the South Pole, in line with the committee's tradition of rewarding new observational methods.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project and its science case; Karle was a decisive figure in the detector and construction, with the collaboration involving hundreds of people. Yoshida contributed to analysis and early development, but the cleanest prize configuration is Halzen with Karle, possibly with a third person; the credited list does not obviously support a larger fair set.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established (5 sigma-plus, with multiple channels). Source identification is at 3-4 sigma individually and the Galactic plane result is recent, but independent confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD is partial. Reasonably mature for the detection, premature for source-population claims.
uncertainties: Individual source associations remain at modest significance.
Credit within a very large collaboration is hard to apportion.
The role of Karle versus Yoshida versus others is from my memory and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts settled a decades-old mystery by placing the bursts at cosmological distances, and thereby revealed the most energetic explosions since the Big Bang. This is a discovery in the clearest sense: a long-standing puzzle answered by observation.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX (Costa, Frontera) delivered the arcminute X-ray localizations and the first afterglow in 1997; Kulkarni led the optical and radio follow-up and redshift work that established the distance scale. Others (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Piro, Metzger and colleagues) were also decisive, so the fair three is debatable, and van Paradijs is deceased.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than 25 years of confirmation, with a developed physical picture (fireball/afterglow), connection to supernovae and to neutron-star mergers via GW170817.
uncertainties: Credit is contested among several teams.
The Swift era and the later short-burst and kilonova work may be seen as the more natural subject.
Gehrels and others also relevant; I am recalling history without verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the subsequent experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created an entire field of moire materials with tunable strong correlation. A prediction followed by a striking experimental confirmation fits my preference for theory that nature answers.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative continuum-model prediction (2011); Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators found the correlated and superconducting states (2018). Cao is the first author of the experiments but is not in the credited names, and Dean, Mak, Shan and others have extended the work. The three credited names make a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many laboratories, and the physical picture is developing quickly. However, the origin of superconductivity remains debated, and the field is only about eight years old.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is unresolved.
The exclusion of Cao and others from the credited set could complicate fairness.
May be premature compared to long-established candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators reshaped the classification of electronic phases by topology, with a theory (Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) confirmed by the HgTe transport experiments and ARPES on Bi-based materials. Concepts have spread into photonics, cold atoms and mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the Z2 invariant and the graphene QSH proposal; Molenkamp's group made the decisive HgTe edge-transport observation. Hasan was key on the three-dimensional materials via ARPES, while Zhang (deceased) and Bernevig-Hughes are not in this list, so the allocation is knotty.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and stable over fifteen years, with a mature field, though technological payoff is modest.
uncertainties: The 3D topological insulator and quantum spin Hall parts are a compound discovery, and the best three may differ.
Overlap with the other topological-matter candidates (B003, B020, B024) and the committee's topological-matter fatigue after the 2016 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation and the quantum origin of cosmological fluctuations explain the flatness, horizon and structure puzzles, and the near scale-invariant spectrum measured in the CMB is a striking success. The idea has shaped cosmology for forty years.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed inflation, Linde the new and chaotic scenarios, Mukhanov the quantum fluctuation calculation connecting to the CMB. Starobinsky (deceased) and Sato also have priority claims, and the credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: The predictions of nearly scale-invariant adiabatic perturbations are confirmed, but the inflationary mechanism itself, the specific model and primordial gravitational waves remain unconfirmed. I am cautious: the fluctuations spectrum is verified, the paradigm is not uniquely tested, and some of the community challenges it.
uncertainties: No direct evidence for the inflaton or primordial B-modes.
Competing priority claims (Starobinsky) and the problem that the full set of contributors exceeds three.
As a string theorist I am aware that the embedding of inflation in a UV-complete theory is unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have reported evidence of a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, opening the gravitational-wave spectrum at wavelengths of light-years, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries. A new window in gravitation is exactly what I find exciting.
assessment.attribution: The credited names are leaders of pulsar timing programmes (Parkes, EPTA, NANOGrav), but the 2023 evidence came from several collaborations, and the central contributions to the method (Hellings-Downs analysis, Detweiler, Foster-Backer) are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Evidence is at about 3-4 sigma with a Hellings-Downs signature emerging, yet not a firm detection, and the origin (black-hole binaries versus new physics) is open. Premature for now, but a likely candidate in some years.
uncertainties: Significance is below the five-sigma standard.
The astrophysical amplitude is somewhat higher than expected.
Fair credit assignment among large collaborations is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are being used to test fundamental constants, probe gravitational redshift at millimetre scales and prepare for a redefinition of the second. A measurement advance that connects to tests of gravity.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks, and Ye's group pushed the performance to the frontier. The two-person configuration is clean, although Hall and Hansch were already recognised in 2005 for the frequency comb, which was a precondition.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced across several laboratories, with international metrology adoption in progress.
uncertainties: The redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
Competing ion-clock work (Wineland-style, Rosenband and others) may be seen as equally deserving.
Overlap in Ye's name with B005 raises allocation questions.
